title: the board shows which project
acceptance: Implements the board half of design.md section 15.4. Replay keys tasks, pull requests and decisions by (project, id), so two projects with the same task id never merge into one lane card. Lane cards, crew bubbles and decision cards show a project chip; ?project= filters and its absence shows every project. Merge cards link the pull request on that project's repository.
Chip labels come from the UI dictionaries; a project name is data and is not translated. With only the default project in the log the board renders as it does today.

Implements the board half of design.md section 15.10 (points 3 and 4). Without ?project= the board shows live work and decision cards of several projects at the same time; the deck lists every pending card of every project in one list, oldest request first, and its pending count covers all projects or only the filtered one. Answering one card never changes, removes or reorders another project's pending card. The merge route follows design.md section 5.2's outcome contract: it passes the card's --project to fm-merge.sh, publishes the response with merge running, runs the helper in the background without blocking the server, answers at once, and rewrites the stored record's merge to merged or failed (with the reason) when the helper exits; a failed merge is never retried. A second merge in the same project while one runs is refused with 409 before anything is published or emitted, leaving that card pending; another project's merge runs alongside it. The board accepts both decision-id shapes of section 15.4 (D-<digits> and D-<project>-<task>-<n>) wherever it reads or answers a decision; since D-1015 nothing is renumbered, so no id is resolved through a map. A record left saying merge running is recovered by the board, the only writer of merge, as design.md section 5.2 says: the merge marker records the decision id and the helper's pid and start time; on start and on every poll the board leaves the record running while that helper is alive, and otherwise reads the outcome from a merged event for the card's (project, pr) after the response, then from GitHub's pull request state (MERGED makes it merged; OPEN or CLOSED makes it failed, never retried); if GitHub cannot be read the record stays running, the card says the outcome is unknown and the project's turn stays held.

Tests with two registered projects live at the same time, written to fail first: both projects' lane cards, crew bubbles and pending decision cards (including one merge card each) render together with their chips; answering one project's card leaves the other's pending and in place; while one project's merge helper is still running, the board still serves, that card's record says merge running, and the other project's merge completes; a second merge in the first project is refused with no response file and no decision_made event; the record says merged or failed once the helper exits; a D-<project>-<task>-<n> card is listed and answerable. Recovery tests, also written to fail first, with a gh stub that answers in gh's real JSON shape: a record saying merge running whose helper pid is dead becomes merged after a board restart when the log has the merged event, merged when only GitHub says MERGED, failed when GitHub says OPEN, and stays running and marked unknown when gh fails; a record whose helper is alive is left running; each resolved record frees its project so a next merge there is no longer refused.
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
